scores.evidence: Because Kinesis delivers at least once, this gives an exactly-once effect within the 35-day window.
scores.rationale: Claims about Kinesis semantics, Stripe idempotency keys and Connect direct charges, RLS with transaction-scoped set_config, gapless sequences, and partitioned unique constraints are all accurate, with uncertain vendor behaviors (Stripe Tax on connected accounts, pooler pinning) correctly flagged for spikes rather than asserted.

scores.evidence: If you actually meant "billing for our own multi-tenant SaaS product," stop here... buy Stripe Billing, Chargebee, or Orb
scores.rationale: The central ambiguity is surfaced and resolved explicitly with a fallback recommendation, core billing capabilities are all covered, exclusions are listed with reasons, and the scope is credibly buildable by the stated team.

scores.evidence: One Postgres schema per module... A module only touches its own schema. Other modules call it through its exported TypeScript interface
scores.rationale: Every entity has one writing owner, data flows connect end to end, and cross-cutting choices (RLS tenancy, transactional outbox, idempotency, forward-only state transitions) are applied uniformly with no contradictions found.

scores.evidence: nightly shadow re-rating of 5% of the day's finalised invoices from snapshots (must match exactly)
scores.rationale: The riskiest assumptions are tested in week-1 time-boxed spikes with stated plan-changing outcomes, acceptance gates are checkable (golden suites, isolation harness, shadow cycle with 0 unexplained differences), and validation continues in production via invariants, re-rating and reconciliation.

scores.evidence: Assumption | Impact if wrong | How and when validated
scores.rationale: Every load-bearing assumption is explicit, labeled, paired with its consequence if wrong and a validation method and date, and numeric targets are repeatedly marked as assumptions rather than facts.

scores.evidence: If a call times out, the attempt becomes `unknown`. Nothing retries it until the reconciler has looked it up in Stripe.
scores.rationale: Covers the hard domain failures—duplicate events, worker crash mid-batch, unknown payment outcomes, out-of-order webhooks, tax outage during finalisation, cross-tenant leaks, noisy neighbors, card testing—each with concrete detection, containment and recovery.

scores.evidence: Injected failures in staging (stop aggregator; block Stripe egress) trigger the matching alerts.
scores.rationale: Symptom-based alerts tied to runbooks, demonstrated deploy and rollback, expand/contract migrations, kill switches, restore drills, break-glass access and a billing-day staffing plan are all sized to the stated 6-engineer team.

scores.evidence: Datadog | ≈ $1–2.5k (largest variable; set log index quotas)
scores.rationale: Run costs are itemized as labeled ranges with controls, the largest variable is identified, build cost is expressed via team and milestones, and build-versus-buy trade-offs (Kafka/ClickHouse, Temporal, TigerBeetle, tax vendors) are explicitly weighed.

scores.evidence: Write ADRs for D1, D2, D7, D8, and D9 (the hard-to-reverse ones)... so they can be challenged in week 1
scores.rationale: Every decision carries a reversibility rating and revisit trigger, the hard-to-reverse ones (tenancy model, money representation, numbering, public API) get early validation and ADRs, and exit paths (cells, PspAdapter, TaxProvider, metering split) are concrete.

A modular monolith with one justified separate service, deliberate avoidance of Kafka/ClickHouse/microservices/multi-region at launch, and trigger-based deferrals give the simplest design that still meets the need with a stated growth path.

scores.evidence: T12 ... Test: feed the same batch 3 times, aggregates equal 1×. Kill worker mid-batch, restart, totals correct.
scores.rationale: Tasks T0–T21 have locations, verifiable done-criteria and dependency ordering, spikes state the result that would change the plan, and milestones carry exit criteria, so a team could start on day 1 without redoing the thinking.

checklist.evidence: Money: integer minor units for amounts, numeric(38,12) for unit prices, decimal.js, round once per line half-up
a trigger rejects UPDATE/DELETE on finalised invoice rows and lines... Corrections are credit notes.
The Stripe idempotency key is the payment_attempt.id... INSERT … ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING on psp_events(stripe_event_id)
No card data, ever... Verify the signature... Stay at PCI DSS SAQ A by never touching card data
RLS enabled and forced... isolation test suite in which tenant A tries every endpoint with tenant B's IDs
Unique (tenant_id, event_id, event_date)... The next invoice gets a "prior-period adjustment" line that names the original period.
proration by seconds within each segment... anchors on the 29th–31st, daylight saving and time zones... immutable price versions
take the next number from the per-tenant sequence (UPDATE invoice_sequences … RETURNING makes it gapless)... Tax behind TaxProvider
a retry schedule per tenant (default: days 1, 3, 5, 7), then a terminal action (cancel subscription, mark uncollectible, or leave past_due)
Reconciliation (nightly): compare Stripe charges and refunds per connected account against payment_attempts... A finance or ops person reviews the reconciliation report daily
Non-goals (v1): ... an entitlements or feature-flag service... Real-time prepaid credit burn-down, spend alerts, entitlements API | 2+ partners require it
the right call is to buy Stripe Billing, Chargebee, or Orb and build a thin layer for entitlements and usage forwarding

traps.evidence: floats (rejected); integer only; this [integer minor units + decimal.js]
Finalised invoices immutable; corrections only via credit notes; gapless per-tenant numbering
it retries step 2 with the same idempotency key, so Stripe never creates a duplicate charge
Card data | none (Stripe tokens only) | SAQ A scope
Tenant scoping is enforced in the database by RLS... CI schema lint fails if any table... lacks tenant_id, RLS

note: An exemplary plan: technically precise on billing's hard parts (idempotent money movement, exact-once metering, enforced tenancy, immutable records), with explicit labeled assumptions, early risk-targeted spikes, shadow-billing validation gates, and a day-1-actionable build sequence; the only soft spot is entitlement decoupling, which is explicitly deferred rather than designed.
